section.content: The invention discloses an aqueous binder and a secondary battery. The adhesive comprises at least two monomer units, wherein one monomer unit is a vinyl unsaturated amide sulfonic acid monomer unit, and the other monomer unit is a vinyl unsaturated silane coupling agent monomer unit, and the vinyl unsaturated amide sulfonic acid monomer unit is a cross-linkable self-repairing and self-healing polymer. Preferably, it has a number average molecular weight greater than or equal to 40 ten thousand. The invention also relates to a secondary battery, which comprises a positive pole piece, a negative pole piece, a separation film and electrolyte, wherein at least one of the positive pole piece, the negative pole piece and the separation film contains the adhesive. Compared with the binder in the prior art, the binder provided by the invention has the advantages of good mechanical property, strong binding capacity and high electrochemical stability.

本发明公开了一种水性粘结剂及二次电池。该粘结剂包含至少两种单体单元，其中一种是乙烯基不饱和酰胺磺酸类单体单元，另一种是乙烯基不饱和硅烷偶联剂类单体单元，它是一种可交联并具有自修复性、自愈合性的聚合物。优选地，其数均分子量大于或等于40万。本发明还涉及一种二次电池，包含正极极片、负极极片、隔离膜和电解质，在正极极片、负极极片、隔离膜中至少一种含有本发明的粘结剂。本发明所述的粘结剂相比于现有技术中的粘结剂，机械性能好，粘结能力强，电化学稳定性高。

Water-based binder and secondary batteryTechnical Field

The invention relates to the technical field of secondary batteries, in particular to an aqueous binder for a battery and a secondary battery containing the same, especially a silicon-based negative electrode secondary battery.

Background

In recent 20 years, secondary batteries have received much attention due to their high energy density and long cycle life, and have become a major focus in the field of new energy research. With the popularization and rapid development of electric vehicles, higher demands are made on the long life and high energy density of secondary batteries. The negative electrode material of the current commercial secondary battery is graphite or various carbon materials synthesized by taking graphite as a precursor. However, the theoretical lithium storage capacity of the system electrode is low (372mAh/g), so that the requirement of high energy density of a power battery cannot be met. Therefore, the development of a novel and reliable secondary battery anode material becomes a technical bottleneck in the development of a high-performance secondary battery.

Silicon has the highest specific capacity (about 4200mAh/g) and relatively low delithiation potential (0.1-0.5V vs. Li/Li) as the negative electrode material of secondary battery+) Moreover, the silicon material has the advantages of abundant sources, low price and the like, and is gradually becoming an ideal secondary battery cathode material. However, under the condition of high lithium intercalation, the silicon material can generate a huge volume effect (400%), which is easy to cause the collapse of the electrode structure and the peeling of the electrode material to cause the loss of the conductive network of the electrode material, thereby causing the rapid capacity attenuation and poor cycle performance of the electrode. Commercialization of silicon-based anode materials has been hampered to some extent.

The binder is an important component of the anode and the cathode of the secondary battery, and plays a role in maintaining the structural integrity of the electrode and ensuring the normal and repeated operation of the battery in the charging and discharging processes. The current binders for silicon-based anode materials are mainly: styrene Butadiene Rubber (SBR); polysaccharide materials such as: sodium Alginate (SA) and sodium carboxymethylcellulose (CMC-Na); polyacrylic acid (PAA); polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF), and the like. The SBR has certain elasticity and can inhibit the volume expansion of the electrode material in the charging and discharging processes, but cannot overcome the huge volume expansion effect of the silicon negative electrode, and the SBR has weak binding capacity, so that the particles and the current collector are not firmly bound, and the risk of cyclic demoulding is caused. SA and CMC-Na can properly improve the cycle performance of the silicon-based negative electrode material, but the mechanical strength of the material is low, and the material is not enough to overcome the huge volume expansion effect of the silicon negative electrode. PVDF is easy to swell in electrolyte, so that the adhesive force of an electrode plate is greatly reduced, and the electrode structure is difficult to recover. And PVDF is a solvent-type binder, and does not meet the development trend of the existing water-based negative electrode binder. The PAA reacts with lithium ions in the process of electrode de-intercalation, so that the capacity is low, and the PAA is brittle and the fatigue resistance of the material is poor. The negative electrode binder with high adhesion and fatigue resistance and the corresponding negative electrode plate with high performance become the technical bottleneck for developing the next generation of high energy density secondary battery. Therefore, in order to maximally suppress the volume expansion effect of the silicon-based material during the lithium deintercalation process and obtain a lithium battery with excellent cycle performance and high energy density, the high-strength binder is a very critical factor for the normal operation and performance improvement of the silicon-based secondary battery.

The invention is specially provided for overcoming the defects in the prior art.

Disclosure of Invention

The primary object of the present invention is to provide an aqueous binder having high adhesion and fatigue resistance suitable for secondary batteries, particularly for secondary batteries using a silicon-based material as a negative electrode active material.

A second object of the present invention is to provide a secondary battery having good performance.

The technical scheme of the invention is as follows:

an aqueous binder which is a polymer comprising at least two monomer units, wherein one monomer unit is a unit represented by the formula (I) containing both a sulfonic acid group and an amide group, and the other monomer unit is a unit represented by the formula (II) -1 or the formula (II) -2,

wherein,

in the formula (I), R1Selected from H, C1, 2,3, 4, 5 or 6 straight chain or branched alkyl or substituted alkylnH2nIs a straight-chain or branched alkylene group with n being 1,2, 3, 4, 5 or 6, X is selected from hydrogen ions, lithium ions, sodium ions, potassium ions, rubidium ions, cesium ions or ammonium ions, wherein the alkyl has 1,2 or 3 substituents selected from halogen and C1-4Alkyl or C1-4A substituent of an alkoxy group;

in the structural formula (II) -1, R1Selected from H, straight chain or branched chain alkyl or substituted alkyl with 1,2, 3, 4, 5 or 6 carbon atoms, R2Selected from phenyl or substituted phenyl, straight chain or branched chain alkanoyl or substituted alkanoyl with total carbon atoms of 1,2, 3, 4, 5 or 6,Benzoyl or substituted benzoyl wherein the alkyl, phenyl, benzoyl and alkanoyl have 1,2 or 3 substituents selected from halogen, C1-4Alkyl or C1-4A substituent of an alkoxy group;

wherein R in the structural formula (I)1With R in the formula (II) -11R in the structural formula (II) -21Are each independently selected.

In some preferred embodiments of the present invention, the mole percentage of structural units represented by structural formula (I) in the binder is 30% to 90%, more preferably 50% to 80%; the structural units represented by the structural formula (II) -1 or the structural formula (II) -2 account for 5 to 40 mol%, more preferably 10 to 30 mol% of the binder (when the binder contains both the structural formula (II) -1 unit and the structural formula (II) -2 unit, the sum of the mol% of the two units is 5 to 40 mol%, preferably 10 to 30 mol%). When the mole percentage of the structural formula (I) in the structure of the adhesive is in the above range, the adhesive can achieve the best self-healing effect; when the mole percentage of the structural formula (II) -1 or the structural formula (II) -2 in the structure of the binder is in the above range, the crosslinking effect of the binder is the best. As the second component, it is preferable to use a structural unit having a structure of the formula (II) -1.

In some embodiments, the mole percentage of structural units of formula (I) in the binder can have an upper limit of 90%, 80%, 75%, 70%, 65%, etc., and a lower limit of 30%, 32%, 35%, 40%, etc. Therefore, the mole percentage of the structural unit shown in the structural formula (I) in the binder can be 40-80%, 35-75% and the like.

In some embodiments, the mole percentage of the structural unit represented by structural formula (II) -1 or structural formula (II) -2 in the binder may be 40%, 33%, 21%, 15%, etc. at the upper limit and 5%, 6%, 8%, 10%, etc. at the lower limit. Therefore, the mole percentage of the structural unit shown in the structural formula (II) -1 or the structural formula (II) -2 in the binder can be 5-18%, 6-33% and the like.

It will be understood by those skilled in the art that the binder of the present invention may contain, in addition to the unit of formula (I), the unit of formula (II) -1 or (II) -2, other kinds of units as necessary, as long as they are copolymerizable with the unit of formula (I), the unit of formula (II) -1 or (II) -2 without adversely affecting the properties of the binder. In order to further enhance the binding property, preferably, the binder further comprises units shown in structural formula (III) -1 or/and structural formula (III) -2, and the molar percentage of the (III) -1 or/and (III) -2 units in the binder is 5-30%.

R in the formula (III) -11And R2With R in the formula (II) -11And R2R in the formula (III) -2 is defined as1And R3With R in the formula (II) -21And R3The definitions are the same.

In other embodiments, the binder of the present invention is composed of a unit of structural formula (I) and a unit of structural formula (II) -1 and/or a unit of structural formula (II) -2, and may be composed of a unit of structural formula (I) and a unit of structural formula (II) -1, a unit of structural formula (I) and a unit of structural formula (II) -2, or a unit of structural formula (I), a unit of structural formula (II) -1, and a unit of structural formula (II) -2. At this time, the sum of the mole percentage of the unit of structural formula (I) and the mole percentage of the unit of structural formula (II) -1 and/or the unit of structural formula (II) -2 in the binder should be 100%. In the case where the binder of the present invention is a terpolymer as described above, the sum of the molar percentages of both the units of formula (II) -1 and the units of formula (II) -2 satisfies the condition specified above, i.e., constitutes from 5 to 40%, more preferably from 10 to 30%, of the molar percentage of the binder.

In some preferred embodiments of the present invention, the number average molecular weight of the binder is equal to or greater than 40 ten thousand, preferably 40 ten thousand to 160 ten thousand, and more preferably 40 ten thousand to 100 ten thousand.

The binder polymer of the present invention has a simple structure, and can be easily prepared by those skilled in the art according to its structure, for example, by the most common solution polymerization method. The preparation process is simple, easy to control, high in feasibility, less in environmental pollution and suitable for industrial mass production. Specifically, the binder of the present invention can be prepared by the following method: mixing a vinyl unsaturated amide sulfonic acid monomer (used for forming a monomer unit of a structural formula (I)), a vinyl silane coupling agent (used for forming a monomer unit of a structural formula (II) -1 or a structural formula (II) -2) and an optional polymerization initiator, continuously and slowly dripping the mixture into a solvent under an inert gas atmosphere, and carrying out polymerization reaction at 60-120 ℃ for 8-28 h to prepare the binder.

Wherein the feeding molar ratio of the vinyl unsaturated amide sulfonic acid monomer to the vinyl silane coupling agent monomer is preferably 3: 1 to 20: the binder obtained in the range has good water solubility and stability, and the adhesion performance and the crosslinking performance between the binder and a negative electrode active material are optimal. Wherein the reaction solvent is a mixture of one of tetrahydrofuran, N-dimethylformamide, N-dimethylacetamide, dimethyl sulfoxide, methanol, dioxane, acetone and acetonitrile and water, and the ratio of the mass of the solvent to the sum of the mass of the vinyl unsaturated amide sulfonic acid monomer and the mass of the vinyl silane coupling agent monomer can be 100 (50-200).

Wherein the optional polymerization initiator is for example azobisisobutyronitrile, benzoyl peroxide, 4' -azobis (4-cyanovaleric acid), most preferably benzoyl peroxide. The mass of the polymerization initiator is 0.1 to 3% of the sum of the mass of the vinyl unsaturated amide sulfonic acid monomer and the mass of the vinyl silane coupling agent monomer, and most preferably 0.5 to 2%. The inert gas is argon or nitrogen, most preferably argon. The polymerization temperature is most preferably in the range of 80 to 100 ℃ and the polymerization time is most preferably 12 to 24 hours.

The adhesive is prepared by adopting the solvent system and the most preferable polymerization initiator, proportion and the most preferable polymerization atmosphere, temperature and time, and the molecular weight range can be controlled within the preferable range of 40-160 ten thousand due to the proper type and proportion of the initiator and mild reaction conditions.

The adhesive can be used as an adhesive for a positive pole piece, a negative pole piece or an isolating membrane of a secondary battery. The adhesive of the invention is particularly preferable as the adhesive of the negative pole piece (especially the negative pole piece made of silicon-based material) of the secondary battery, because the problems caused by the adhesion of the negative pole piece in the secondary battery are more remarkable.

Therefore, the invention also relates to a secondary battery (preferably a lithium ion secondary battery) comprising a positive pole piece, a negative pole piece, a separation film and an electrolyte, wherein at least one of the positive pole piece, the negative pole piece and the separation film contains the binder.

Methods for preparing battery anodes using binders are well known to those skilled in the art. Preferably, one method for preparing the negative electrode plate by using the binder disclosed by the invention is as follows:

the binder, the conductive agent and the active substance are mixed in deionized water to obtain slurry, and the obtained slurry is coated on a current collector to prepare the negative pole piece.

In some embodiments, the negative electrode plate contains the binder of the present invention, specifically, the negative electrode plate includes a negative electrode current collector and a negative electrode active material coating, and the negative electrode active material coating includes a conductive agent, a negative electrode active material and the binder of the present invention. Preferably, the mass percentage of the binder in the secondary battery negative pole piece in the negative active material coating formed by the conductive agent, the negative active material and the binder is 2-20%.

The other method for preparing the negative pole piece by using the binder disclosed by the invention comprises the following steps of: the binder is directly coated on the current collector to form a current collector coating.

In some embodiments, the negative electrode plate contains the binder of the present invention, specifically, the negative electrode plate includes a negative electrode current collector and a negative electrode active material coating, a coating is disposed between the negative electrode current collector and the negative electrode active material coating, and the coating includes the binder of the present invention.

The conductive agent is not limited and comprises one or more of carbon nano tube, conductive carbon black, carbon fiber and graphene.

The active material is not limited and may be a graphite material or a silicon-based material, but the binder of the present invention is particularly suitable for a silicon-based material negative electrode. Therefore, the preferable negative electrode active material includes one or more of amorphous silicon, carbon-coated amorphous silicon particles, polycrystalline silicon particles, silica particles, or silicon-based alloy powder.

The current collector is not limited, and a copper foil is preferred.

The invention has the beneficial effects that:

the adhesive is an ionic polymer, the side chain of the adhesive contains a sulfonic group structure, and compared with a polyacrylic acid adhesive material used by a traditional silicon-based negative electrode, the acidity of the sulfonic group is stronger than that of a carboxylic group, and ions are more easily dissociated. Therefore, the mobility is high, the conductivity is good, and the electrode polarization is effectively reduced. Therefore, the dynamic performance of the conventional silicon-based negative electrode binder is improved, and particularly the problem of rapid battery capacity attenuation caused by high-rate charge and discharge is solved.

The O of the-S ═ O-bond in the ionic sulfonic acid group contained in the binder of the present invention can form a strong hydrogen bonding action with the H of the N — H bond in the amide group, so that the polymer molecular chains form a three-dimensional hydrogen bonding network structure, and have self-crosslinking, self-repairing and self-healing properties (see the schematic diagram of fig. 1). When the silicon-based negative electrode is subjected to larger volume expansion or contraction change due to charge and discharge and the like, the binder material still has excellent adhesion and mechanical strength, even if the microscopic interface of the material is fractured due to repeated volume expansion, hydrogen bond self-repairing damaged parts can be quickly formed by the contact between the interfaces after the material is contracted, and the fatigue resistance of the binder material is further improved, so that the problems of binder peeling and conductive network damage caused by the deterioration or failure of the adhesion performance of the binder due to the volume change of the silicon-based negative electrode are solved.

The adhesive contains silane coupling groups, the silicon-based negative electrode material is rich in Si-OH groups, the silane coupling agent groups can perform a crosslinking reaction with Si-OH to form stable-Si-O-Si-groups, and a molecular chain of the adhesive is riveted on the surface of an active material in a covalent bond mode to form a compact coating layer (see the schematic diagram of the attached drawing 1). And the Si-OH of the binder can also generate cross-linking reaction to form a covalent bond network structure, thereby further enhancing the mechanical property of the material. Therefore, the problem that the bonding agent is separated from the interface layer of the active material due to severe volume change of silicon particles in the circulation process of the silicon-based negative electrode is solved, and the circulation stability and the coulombic efficiency of the battery are improved.

Therefore, in the binder of the present invention, one structural unit imparts self-healing property to the binder, and the other structural unit enhances the binding force of the binder, so that the secondary battery containing the binder has very excellent overall performance due to the unique structural composition and the cooperation of the two structural units. The binder and the negative active material are subjected to a crosslinking reaction to form a three-dimensional network structure, and the material has self-crosslinking property and self-healing property, so that the large-volume change caused by the negative active material in the charging and discharging process can be effectively inhibited, the strength of the material is maintained, the capacity of the secondary battery can be remarkably improved, the cycle life is prolonged, and the cycle expansion force is reduced. This characteristic makes the aqueous binder of the present invention particularly suitable for secondary batteries having a silicon-based material as a negative electrode, and can significantly improve the performance of the battery. In addition, the binder material for the secondary battery is simple in preparation process, and can be prepared by the most common solution polymerization method, so that the binder material has the advantages of easiness in process control, high feasibility, less environmental pollution, suitability for industrial mass production and the like.

Examples

The invention will be further illustrated with reference to specific examples. It should be understood that these examples are for illustrative purposes only and are not intended to limit the scope of the present application. In practice, the invention will be understood to be applicable to all modifications and variations of the invention as may be suggested to those skilled in the art.

First, examples 1 to 4

1. Preparation of the binder:

adding a certain amount of solvent (mixed solvent of N, N-dimethylformamide and water) into a four-neck flask provided with a condenser tube, a stirrer and a thermometer, introducing argon for 30min, and heating to 90 ℃; dropping a mixture of vinyl unsaturated sulfonic acid amide monomers (monomer units shown in formula (I)), vinyl unsaturated silane coupling agents (monomer units shown in formula (II) -1 or formula (II) -2) and benzoyl peroxide in a feeding amount at a constant speed under the protection of argon; after the dropwise addition, the reaction is carried out for a set time under the condition of heat preservation, and the solution is cooled to room temperature and then is spray-dried to obtain the solid powder of the binder. 2. Preparation of lithium ion secondary battery:

the binders of examples 1 to 4 prepared above were used to prepare corresponding lithium ion secondary batteries. The lithium ion secondary battery comprises a positive pole piece, a negative pole piece, an isolating membrane and electrolyte, and the material selection and preparation processes of all the components are briefly described as follows.

1) The positive pole piece comprises a positive current collector and a positive active material layer coated on the positive current collector. The positive current collector is an aluminum foil, and the positive active material layer comprises the following components in percentage by mass:

the positive electrode active material is LiNi1/3Mn1/3Co1/3O294.0 percent;

the positive electrode binder is polyvinylidene fluoride, and the content is 3.0%;

the positive electrode conductive agent is acetylene black with the content of 3.0 percent;

the positive current collector is aluminum foil with a thickness of 14 um.

2) The negative pole piece comprises a negative pole current collector and a negative pole active material layer coated on the negative pole current collector. The negative current collector is a copper foil, and the negative active material layer comprises the following components:

the negative active material is silicon-based alloy S14(MK Electron Co. Ltd.), and the content is 95.0 percent;

the negative conductive agent is conductive carbon black with the content of 2.0 percent.

The negative electrode binders were the polymer materials prepared in examples 1 to 4, respectively, and the content was 3%;

the negative current collector is a copper foil with the thickness of 10 um.

3) The isolating membrane is a polyethylene porous film with the thickness of 14 um.

4) The electrolyte comprises an organic solvent and lithium salt, wherein the organic solvent is a mixture of diethyl carbonate, dimethyl carbonate and ethylene carbonate, and the volume ratio of the three solvents is 1: 1: 1, the lithium salt is LiPF6The concentration is 1 mol/L.

5) Preparing a lithium ion full battery:

preparing a positive pole piece: mixing 94.0% LiNi1/3Mn1/3Co1/3O2Adding 3.0% of polyvinylidene fluoride and 3.0% of acetylene black into an N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) solvent system, fully stirring and uniformly mixing, coating on an aluminum foil, drying, and cold pressing to obtain the positive pole piece.
